native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: In unadjusted bivariate comparisons, individuals with a criminal record (ever jailed) had significantly lower wealth compared to those without in all three surveyed years: 1985, 1990, and 1996 (Welch t-test p < 1e-18, Mann-Whitney U p < 1e-10). When controlling for race and sex using multivariable regression, the wealth penalty associated with incarceration was statistically significant in 1990 (p = 0.007) and 1996 (p < 0.001), but not statistically significant in 1985 (p = 0.112), with the wealth disparity widening substantially over time.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv and validated sample sizes across ever_jailed categories. 2. Computed parametric (mean, std) and non-parametric (median, IQR) summary statistics across 1985, 1990, and 1996. 3. Conducted Welch two-sample t-tests and Mann-Whitney U tests for unadjusted wealth comparison between jailed and non-jailed cohorts. 4. Fitted multivariable OLS regression models controlling for race and sex for each year to assess adjusted effect sizes and significance. 5. Synthesized empirical evidence into a comprehensive natural-language hypothesis.
